question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-3,0]\times [-3,0]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-{y}^{2}+3 \\ {x}^{2}y-2x+5\end{aligned}]. $$ Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts with ${x}_{0}=[-2,\,-2]^{T}.$ Round your answer to three decimal places (if needed).
${x}_{1}≈[$ {{field-1}} $]$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{4}-{y}^{2}+3) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{4}-{y}^{2}+3) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y-2x+5) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y-2x+5)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3} & -2y \\ 2xy-2 & {x}^{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3} & -2y \\ 2xy-2 & {x}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-{y}^{2}+3 \\ {x}^{2}y-2x+5\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-{[\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3} & -2y \\ 2xy-2 & {x}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-{y}^{2}+3 \\ {x}^{2}y-2x+5\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}4(-2)^{3} & -2(-2) \\ 2(-2)(-2)-2 & (-2)^{2}\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(-2)^{4}-(-2)^{2}+3 \\ (-2)^{2}(-2)-2(-2)+5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-32 & 4 \\ 6 & 4\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}15 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(-32)\cdot 4-4\cdot 6}[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ -6 & -32\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}15 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{152}[\begin{aligned}56 \\ -122\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}-1.632 \\ -2.803\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
